original_question: What is the name of the amino acid transporter protein encoded by the gene which is mutated in lysinuric protein intolerance?

final_qi.question: What is the name of the amino acid transporter protein encoded by the gene which is mutated in lysinuric protein intolerance?
final_qi.long_answer: Lysinuric protein intolerance is caused by loss-of-function mutations in the SLC7A7 gene. This gene encodes the light-chain subunit of the system y+L transporter, officially named y+L amino acid transporter 1 (y+LAT1), which mediates basolateral efflux of cationic amino acids (lysine, arginine, ornithine) in intestinal and renal epithelial cells. Defective y+LAT1 impairs reabsorption and absorption of these amino acids, producing the clinical phenotype of lysinuric protein intolerance.

0.question: Which gene is mutated in lysinuric protein intolerance?

final_answer.long_answer: Lysinuric protein intolerance is caused by mutations in the SLC7A7 gene. This gene encodes y+L amino acid transporter 1 (y+LAT-1), the basolateral membrane subunit of the heterodimeric transporter responsible for exporting cationic amino acids such as lysine, arginine and ornithine from intestinal and renal epithelial cells. Loss-of-function mutations in SLC7A7/y+LAT-1 impair this transport, leading to the characteristic aminoaciduria and systemic manifestations of the disorder.
